papers.title: Decomposition of Scaled Relative Graphs: A Mixed Systems Approach
papers.authors: S van den Eijnden - IEEE Control Systems Letters, 2026
papers.abstract: Scaled relative graphs provide a promising framework for graphical nonlinear system analysis, extending the classical Nyquist diagram for linear time-invariant systems. Unlike the Nyquist diagram, however, scaled relative graphs do not preserve information linking specific input regimes to corresponding output behaviours, which can lead to conservatism in feedback analysis. In this paper, we present a refined scaled relative graph frame-work that explicitly accounts for input-specific system …

papers.title: From Grid Search to Modern Deterministic Approaches: a Brief Review of Hyper-parameter Optimisation in Deep and Foundation Models Era
papers.abstract: As deep and machine learning systems grow in scale and are deployed in sensitive, high-stakes environments, the need for reliable and fully reproducible model tuning has never been greater. This paper presents a clear and structured overview of Deterministic Hyper-parameter Optimisation (DHPO), covering four key families of methods: Direct Search, Surrogate-based, Hyper-gradient, and Multi-Fidelity approaches. We frame DHPO within a reproducible bilevel optimisation setting and …

papers.title: Tikhonov regularization of monotone operator flows not only ensures strong convergence of the trajectories but also speeds up the vanishing of the residuals
papers.authors: RI Boţ, DK Nguyen - Journal of Complexity, 2026
papers.abstract: In the framework of real Hilbert spaces, we study first-order dynamical systems augmented with a Tikhonov regularization term associated with an equation governed by a monotone and continuous operator. We show that, besides guaranteeing the strong convergence of the trajectory to the minimum norm solution, convergence rates for both the velocity norm and the residual norm can be derived in terms of the regularization function.
